mainTopic: Rabbinic penalties (קנס): property versus body, the wording of רבי אליעזר's ruling, and whether a son inherits his father's קנס
overview: This amud opens by finishing a contradiction. רבי אליעזר penalizes forever a person who blemishes a בכור. Yet he lets a person who cut off his בהרת become טהור once a new נגע appears. רבה and רב יוסף answer that רבי אליעזר is stricter about property (ממונו) than about the body (גופו), because people are more tempted to cheat with their property. רבא adds that the רבנן also need an explanation, and he gives one: they always penalize through the very act the person did, so the blemish or the cutting simply does not count. רב פפא then asks whether רבי אליעזר's ruling reads 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר'. The difference matters for a חתן whose new נגע is not examined during his wedding week, and the question ends in תיקו. Next, רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether the penalty for blemishing a בכור passes to the son after the father dies. רבי זירא proves from a field improved during שביעית that the רבנן fined the father personally, not his son. The amud ends as אביי begins a tradition of his own, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the contradicting source: cutting off a leprous spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about צרעת. In it, רבי אליעזר lets a person who deliberately cut off his בהרת become טהור once a new נגע appears. This contradicts his permanent penalty in the case of the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the spot got cut off by accident, the person is pure. If he cut it off on purpose, רבי אליעזר says: once another leprous spot develops on him, he becomes pure from it. The חכמים say: he stays impure until the leprosy spreads over his whole body, or unless his spot had already shrunk to less than the size of a split bean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה about צרעת that it brought to challenge רבי אליעזר. In this case, רבי אליעזר's penalty for cheating the system eventually ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בכור case, רבי אליעזר said the cheater may never benefit, even after a new blemish appears. Here, a person who cheated by cutting off his בהרת gets a way out: once a new נגע appears and is judged, he can become טהור. So רבי אליעזר seems lenient here and strict there, which looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: It got cut off (by itself or by accident)
The leprosy spreads over his entire body (which makes him טהור)
The size of a split bean, the minimum size for a נגע

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic about צרעת. The גמרא is quoting this משנה only to point out a contradiction in רבי אליעזר's approach to penalties (קנס). The real question is: why is his penalty permanent for the בכור but limited here?

phrases.english: and it got cut off — he is pure,
phrases.notes: Accidental removal, so there is no penalty.

phrases.english: if he cut it off intentionally —
phrases.notes: He removed the spot to make himself pure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
when another leprous mark develops on him
phrases.notes: His status will be judged based on the new mark.

phrases.english: he will become pure from it.
phrases.notes: So the penalty has an end point.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: not until it spreads over his entire body,
phrases.notes: Leprosy covering the whole body is a sign of purity.

phrases.english: or unless his spot had shrunk to less than a split bean!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks the end of the quoted source, which completes the contradiction.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְצָצָה מִתְכַּוֵּין — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לִכְשֶׁיִּוָּלֵד לוֹ נֶגַע אַחֵר יִטְהַר הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradicting source (רמינהו) that began on the previous amud, set against רבי אליעזר's ruling about צורם באוזן הבכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's permanent penalty for one who blemishes a בכור (לא ישחט עולמית).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר lets someone who cheated with צרעת become טהור once a new נגע appears, why doesn't he let someone who cheated with a בכור slaughter it once a new blemish appears?

steps.title: Penalty on property versus penalty on the body
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף answer that רבי אליעזר imposes his strong penalty only in matters of a person's property, not in matters of his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: when רבי אליעזר penalizes, it is with regard to a person's property. With regard to his body, he does not penalize that way.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give the same answer to resolve the contradiction. The בכור is property, while צרעת is on the body, and רבי אליעזר treats these differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are not contradictory, because they belong to different categories. A permanent קנס is used for ממונו (the בכור animal). For גופו (a spot on one's skin), רבי אליעזר still penalizes, but only in a limited way.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them (said the same thing)

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
when Rabbi Eliezer penalizes, it is regarding his property,
phrases.notes: This refers to the בכור, which is an animal the owner owns.

phrases.english: regarding his body he does not penalize (that way).
phrases.notes: This refers to צרעת, which is on the person's own skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָנֵיס רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּמָמוֹנוֹ, בְּגוּפוֹ לָא קָנֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): property versus body.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner assumed רבי אליעזר applies one uniform level of penalty to everyone who cheats the system.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר's severe, permanent קנס applies only to cheating with one's property (ממונו), not to cheating with one's body (גופו).

steps.title: Why property needs a stronger penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasoning. People are likely to damage their property to gain from it, so a strong deterrent is needed. People are not likely to cut their own bodies, so a lighter penalty is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his property, there is reason to say he will come to do it. With his body, is there really reason to say he will come to do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the logic behind the answer of רבה and רב יוסף. It does this by comparing how tempting each act is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic קנס is meant to stop people from doing something. Blemishing a בכור is easy and risk-free for the owner, so a harsh, permanent penalty is needed to stop it. Cutting one's own skin is painful and unlikely, and the person may never develop a new נגע anyway. So a limited penalty is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to do it
Is there really reason to say? (a rhetorical question expecting the answer 'no')

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר sets the size of a קנס by how tempting the wrongdoing is. Cheating with property (a בכור) is tempting and easy, so it gets a permanent penalty. Cheating with one's body (צרעת) is unlikely, so it gets a limited penalty.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general principle about rabbinic penalties: the strength of a קנס matches how likely people are to commit the act. This explains why חז"ל are stricter in some cases than others.

phrases.english: His property — there is reason to say
phrases.notes: A בכור cannot be used until it gets a blemish, so the owner loses nothing by causing one.

phrases.english: that he will come to do it,
phrases.notes: So a strong deterrent is needed.

phrases.english: his body — is there reason to say
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The expected answer is no.

phrases.english: that he will come to do it?
phrases.notes: People rarely cut their own skin, so a lighter penalty is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָמוֹנוֹ — אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר דְּאָתֵי לְמֶיעְבַּד, גּוּפוֹ — מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר דְּאָתֵי לְמֶיעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the distinction that רבה and רב יוסף drew in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the distinction, based on how likely people are to commit each act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the distinction between property and body is arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The distinction is based on deterrence. Property is tempting to tamper with, so it needs a strong קנס. The body is not, so a limited קנס is enough.

steps.title: רבא: The Rabbis Also Seem to Contradict Themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the analysis so far has been one-sided. If רבי אליעזר's two rulings need to be reconciled, so do the רבנן's two rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it only that רבי אליעזר contradicts רבי אליעזר, while the רבנן do not contradict the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that the רבנן also look inconsistent between the two משניות. So the גמרא's discussion is incomplete if it only deals with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the בכור, the רבנן are lenient: if a new, natural blemish appears, the animal may be slaughtered. With the בהרת, they are strict and keep the person טמא much longer. That is the reverse of רבי אליעזר's pattern, so the רבנן need an explanation just as much as he does.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי אליעזר
'Against'; used when comparing one ruling to another

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs. רבי אליעזר is strict with the בכור and lenient with the בהרת. The רבנן are the opposite: lenient with the בכור and strict with the בהרת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is Rabbi Eliezer against Rabbi Eliezer difficult,
phrases.notes: This refers to the בכור ruling compared with the בהרת ruling.

phrases.english: while the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. Of course the רבנן also need to be explained.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the contradiction from Step 1 so that it also covers the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the רבנן between the בכור case and the בהרת case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן give a limited penalty for the בכור but a long-lasting penalty for the בהרת. The property-versus-body answer does not explain this, because it would predict the opposite pattern.

steps.title: Both Opinions Are Consistent: Penalize Him for What He Did
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a solution for both sides. רבי אליעזר is explained as before. The רבנן follow one rule: the penalty targets the specific act he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אליעזר against רבי אליעזר is not difficult, as we explained. The רבנן against the רבנן is also not difficult. Here they penalized him for what he did, and there they penalized him for what he did.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction in the רבנן's rulings. He states a single principle that fits both of their rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר stays with the earlier answer: property is treated differently from the body. For the רבנן, the principle is that the penalty undoes the benefit of the specific improper act. The next step explains how this works in each case.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Eliezer against Rabbi Eliezer is not difficult,
as we answered.
phrases.notes: This means the property-versus-body distinction from Steps 2 and 3.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult:
here they penalized him for what he did,
phrases.notes: In the בכור case.

phrases.english: and here they penalized him for what he did.
phrases.notes: In the בהרת case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא raised in Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A single unifying principle for the רבנן's two rulings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed to treat the two cases with different levels of strictness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן always penalize through the exact act the person did, so the penalty's length depends on what that act was meant to achieve.

steps.title: How the Penalty Matches the Act in Each Case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the principle. With the בכור, he wanted to permit the animal through this blemish, so this blemish never counts. With the בהרת, he wanted to become טהור through this cutting, so this cutting never counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through what did he intend to permit the animal? Through this blemish. So the רבנן penalized him regarding this blemish: through this blemish it will not become permitted to him. And here too they penalized him for what he did. He intended to make himself טהור through this cutting, so the רבנן penalized him regarding this cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the rule 'penalize him for what he did' works out in each of the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the בכור, his self-made blemish is ignored, but a new natural blemish still permits the animal, so the penalty looks short. With the בהרת, the cutting is ignored, so it is as if the נגע were still there, and he stays טמא for a long time. The principle is the same in both cases; only the results look different.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's rule is to cancel the effect of the improper act itself. The bad blemish does not count, and the bad cutting does not count. The severity looks different only because the two acts aimed at different results.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic idea of קנס: the penalty often works by ignoring the forbidden act, not by imposing a fixed punishment.

phrases.english: Through what did he intend to permit it?
Through this blemish.
So the Rabbis penalized him regarding this blemish,
meaning that through this blemish it will not be permitted to him.
phrases.notes: A later natural blemish still permits the animal.

phrases.english: And here too they penalized him for what he did:
he intended to make himself pure through this cutting,
so the Rabbis penalized him regarding this cutting.
phrases.notes: The cutting is ignored, so he stays טמא as if the נגע were still there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle stated in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the unifying principle to each case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן are consistent: the act itself is cancelled, and the different results come from what each act was meant to achieve.

steps.title: רב פפא: Is the Text 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר'?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about the exact wording of רבי אליעזר's ruling in the בהרת case: 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: Did we learn 'יטהר', or did we learn 'ויטהר'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the exact wording of רבי אליעזר's ruling. This line sets up a discussion that continues later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יטהר' would mean he becomes טהור from the first נגע as soon as the second one appears. 'ויטהר' would mean he stays טמא from the first until the second נגע is itself declared טהור. So the difference of one letter decides how long the penalty lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he will become טהור' (only after the second נגע is cleared)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about spelling for its own sake. The extra ו changes when he actually becomes טהור.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Did we learn 'yit'har' (he will become pure),
or did we learn 'veyit'har' (and he will become pure)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the contradiction to a question about the wording of רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה from Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה reads 'יטהר' (pure right away) or 'ויטהר' (pure only once the second נגע is cleared).

steps.title: What practical difference does the wording make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between reading 'יטהר' and 'ויטהר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא's wording question matters in real life. This sets up the next step, which gives a case where the two readings lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the two readings seem to give the same result. Once a new נגע appears, he is טמא because of that new נגע anyway, at least until a כהן clears it. So the גמרא needs a case where the first נגע's טומאה matters on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He becomes טהור': as soon as the new נגע appears, he is free of the penalty from the first one
'And he becomes טהור': the penalty lasts until he is also cleared of the new נגע

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two נגעים. The 'first' one is the בהרת he cut off, which brings the penalty טומאה. The 'latter' one is the new נגע that grows later.

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?
phrases.notes: The difference between the readings 'יטהר' and 'ויטהר'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why רב פפא's wording question from step 7 makes any practical difference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'יטהר' and 'ויטהר' lead to different halachic results.

steps.title: The difference shows up with a groom who gets a new נגע
steps.stepSummary: The difference applies to a חתן who develops a new נגע.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a groom on whom a נגע appeared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference shows up with a חתן who finds a new נגע during his wedding week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חתן's new נגע is not examined during the celebration, so the new נגע does not make him טמא yet. That leaves the first נגע's penalty as the only thing that could make him טמא. So here the wording matters.

keyTerms.meaning: A groom, during his seven days of wedding celebration
A mark of צרעת (a skin affliction)

phrases.english: For a groom on whom a mark of leprosy appeared.
phrases.notes: He had cut off his first בהרת, and now a new נגע appeared during his wedding week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by naming the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of a חתן who gets a new נגע during his seven days of celebration.

steps.title: Source: a groom and a person on a festival get a delay
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that a חתן gets seven days, and a person during a רגל gets the whole festival, before a נגע is examined.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a groom on whom a נגע appeared is given seven days, for himself, his cloak, and his garment. Similarly, during a festival, he is given all the days of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה from נגעים as the source showing that a חתן's נגע is not examined during his celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lets a person delay the כהן's inspection, so the נגע cannot make him טמא during this time. The delay covers a נגע on his body and on his clothing. A person during a רגל gets the same kind of delay.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned: a groom on whom a mark of leprosy appeared,
phrases.notes: משנה נגעים 3:2

phrases.english: they give him seven days,
phrases.notes: Before a כהן examines the mark.

phrases.english: for himself, for his cloak, and for his garment,
and similarly on a festival,
they give him all the days of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule behind the case named in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a חתן's new נגע is not examined during his celebration, so it does not make him טמא yet.

steps.title: With the reading יטהר, the groom is fully pure
steps.stepSummary: If the reading is 'יטהר', he is already טהור from the first נגע, and the new one waits until after the celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה reads 'יטהר': from the first נגע he is already טהור, and for the latter one we wait for him the seven days of feasting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the result under the first reading: the חתן is completely טהור during his wedding week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'יטהר', the new נגע appearing ends the penalty from the first one right away. The new נגע is not examined until after the seven days, so nothing makes him טמא during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one (the בהרת he cut off)

phrases.english: If you say we learned 'he becomes pure',
from the first one he has become pure,
phrases.notes: As soon as the new נגע appeared.

phrases.english: for the latter one we wait for him
the seven days of feasting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the חתן rule from step 10 to the 'יטהר' reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With 'יטהר', the חתן is טהור during the seven days.

steps.title: With the reading ויטהר, the groom stays impure
steps.stepSummary: If the reading is 'ויטהר', the delay does not help, because he is still טמא from the first נגע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the משנה reads 'ויטהר': in the end, even though he does not become טמא from the latter נגע, he still stands טמא from the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the opposite result under the second reading: the חתן is still טמא during his wedding week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'ויטהר', the first penalty lasts until he is cleared of the new נגע. A חתן's new נגע cannot be examined until after the celebration, so he cannot be cleared of it yet. He therefore stays טמא from the first נגע, and the delay gives him no benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact case where the two readings disagree. It shows that a single letter ו in רבי אליעזר's ruling decides whether the חתן is טהור or טמא.

phrases.english: But if you say we learned 'and he becomes pure',
in the end,
even though he does not become impure from the latter one,
phrases.notes: Because the new נגע is not examined during the wedding week.

phrases.english: he still remains impure from the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 11 by showing the opposite outcome under 'ויטהר'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With 'ויטהר', the חתן stays טמא from the first נגע during the seven days.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reading is correct and leaves it unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which reading is correct and admits it cannot decide, so the question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether רבי אליעזר said 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר'. So רב פפא's question, together with its practical difference for the חתן, stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא asked whether רבי אליעזר said 'יטהר' (pure from the first נגע as soon as a new one appears) or 'ויטהר' (pure only once cleared of the new one). It matters for a חתן, whose new נגע is not examined during his wedding week. With 'יטהר' he is טהור, and with 'ויטהר' he is טמא. The question ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: What is the answer? Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question from step 7 after both outcomes have been shown.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the reading is 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר' stays unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: Does the son inherit the penalty for a blemished firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether the קנס on a man who cut the ear of a בכור also applies to his son after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: If a man cut the ear of a firstborn animal and then died, do we also penalize his son after him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי ירמיה asks whether a penalty given to a father carries over to his son once the father has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that if someone purposely gives a בכור a blemish by cutting its ear, the רבנן fined him: he may not slaughter it because of that blemish. Now the father has died and the animal belongs to his son. Is the son still stuck with the fine?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question that needs an answer)
Slits or cuts the ear (making a blemish on purpose)
Firstborn male animal, which is holy and given to a כהן
To fine or penalize (a rabbinic penalty)

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether a rabbinic קנס is personal or stays attached to the thing itself, even after it passes to heirs.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
One who slits the ear of a firstborn and then died,
phrases.notes: He made the blemish on purpose so he could slaughter it, and the רבנן fined him.

phrases.english: what is the law about penalizing his son after him?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו in Step 13, going back to the משנה's rule about cutting the ear of a בכור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rabbinic קנס on the one who blemished a בכור also applies to his heir.

steps.title: The slave case is not a proof, because of lost מצוות
steps.stepSummary: With selling a slave to גוים, the son is penalized. But that is because the slave loses מצוות every day, so it cannot decide our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to compare this to one who sold his slave to non-Jews and then died: there the רבנן did penalize his son after him. But that is because every single day the slave is kept away from מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case where the son IS penalized. It then shows why that case is special, so it cannot answer our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who sells his עבד כנעני to a גוי is fined: he must redeem the slave. That fine continues even to his son. But the reason is special. Each day the slave stays with the גוי, he loses מצוות, so the damage keeps happening. With a בכור there is no ongoing damage like that, so the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say (here it introduces a case to compare)
One who sells his slave to non-Jews
Removes or takes him away from
Commandments (the slave is obligated in some מצוות)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר' literally means 'if you should conclude'. It grants the ruling in that other case for the sake of argument and uses it as a comparison. The גמרא then shows that the case does not fit.

phrases.english: If you would say:
One who sells his slave to non-Jews and died —
they penalized his son after him,
phrases.notes: The son must redeem the slave.

phrases.english: because each and every day
he keeps him away from מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר מוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לַגּוֹיִם וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a possible source that would make the son penalized, and shows why it does not fit.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the slave case to show the son is penalized for the בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The slave case has a special reason: the slave loses מצוות every day. That reason does not exist with a בכור.

steps.title: The festival-work case is not a proof, because no sin was done
steps.stepSummary: With planning work for חול המועד, the son is not penalized. But that is because the father never actually did anything forbidden, so it also cannot decide our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to compare this to one who planned his work for חול המועד and then died: there the רבנן did not penalize his son after him. But that is because the father never actually did the forbidden act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the opposite case, where the son is NOT penalized. It shows that this case is also special, so it cannot answer our question either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who sets things up on purpose so he can work on חול המועד is fined. But if he died before the festival, his son is not fined. The reason is that the father never actually broke the rule. Our case is different, because the father really did cut the בכור's ear. So this comparison also fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Purposely planned his work (to fall on the festival)
The middle days of the festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: If you would say:
One who planned his work for the festival and died —
they did not penalize his son after him,
because he never actually did the forbidden act.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר כִּוֵּון מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּמּוֹעֵד וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the opposite comparison, where the son is not penalized, and shows why it also does not fit.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the חול המועד case to show the son is not penalized for the בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the festival case the father never did the forbidden act. With a בכור, the father did make the blemish.

steps.title: Was the fine on the person or on his property?
steps.stepSummary: Since neither comparison works, the גמרא sharpens the question. Did the רבנן fine the father himself, who is gone, or his property, which still exists?
steps.simpleTranslation: So here, what is the law? Did the רבנן penalize him personally, and he is no longer here? Or perhaps the רבנן penalized his property, and that is still here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the question down to its core. Is the קנס aimed at the person or at his money?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the fine was on the father as a person. Then once he died, the fine ends, and the son may slaughter the animal because of its blemish. Suppose instead the fine was on the property, meaning the animal itself. Then it still applies, because the animal is still around in the son's hands. רבי זירא answers this in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not here / it is still here

steps.whatToRemember: The whole question depends on one idea. Is a rabbinic קנס a punishment on the person, which ends when he dies? Or is it on the item, which passes to the heirs together with the fine?

phrases.english: Here, what is the law?
Did the Rabbis penalize him personally,
and he is no longer here,
or perhaps the Rabbis penalized his property,
and that is still here?
phrases.notes: The animal is still around, now owned by the son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both comparisons are pushed aside, the original question is stated again in sharper terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the קנס for blemishing a בכור is on the person or on the property.

steps.title: A proof from the field improved during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי ירמיה that the answer is in a משנה. A field that was only cleared of thorns during שביעית may be planted after the year. A field that was fertilized or used as an animal pen may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it in a משנה. A field that was cleared of thorns during שביעית may be planted after שביעית ends. If it was improved with fertilizer, or animals were penned in it to fertilize it, it may not be planted after שביעית ends.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins answering the question from Step 17 by quoting a משנה about fields worked on during שביעית. This is the base of the proof. The next step finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearing thorns is a small job, so the רבנן did not penalize it. Fertilizing a field or penning animals in it is a real improvement done against the law, so the רבנן fined the owner and forbade him to plant it afterward. This gives us a case with a penalty for a forbidden act, which is just what our בכור question needs.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it already (in a משנה or ברייתא)
The time right after the שמיטה year ends
Was improved, for example with fertilizer
Was used as a pen for animals, so their manure fertilizes the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The ban on planting is not about the שמיטה year itself. It is a penalty that applies AFTER שביעית is over, because the field was improved in a forbidden way.

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
phrases.notes: רבי זירא answering רבי ירמיה

phrases.english: A field that was cleared of thorns during the Sabbatical Year
phrases.notes: A minor kind of work

phrases.english: may be sown after the Sabbatical Year ends;
phrases.notes: No penalty

phrases.english: if it was improved, or was used as an animal pen,
phrases.notes: Real improvements

phrases.english: it may not be sown after the Sabbatical Year ends.
phrases.notes: A קנס on the forbidden improvement

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the sharpened question from Step 17 by bringing a parallel case of a קנס.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a קנס for a forbidden act passes to the son after the father dies
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שביעית (4:2) about a field improved during שביעית

steps.title: If the father died, the son may plant, so the fine was on the person
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי ברבי חנינא has a tradition that if the owner improved the field and then died, his son may plant it. The גמרא concludes that the רבנן fined the father, not his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי ברבי חנינא said: We have a tradition that if he improved it and then died, his son may plant it. This shows that the רבנן fined him, but they did not fine his son.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי זירא's proof. A tradition says the son may plant the field, and from that the גמרא concludes that the penalty was on the father himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן had fined the property, the field would stay forbidden even after the father died. Since the son may plant it, the fine must have been on the father personally, and it ended when he died. This answers the question from Step 17: in the בכור case too, the son should not be penalized.
steps.whatToRemember: A קנס on a forbidden act can be on the person or on the object. The שביעית case shows the רבנן fined the person, so the son is not penalized after the father dies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives an answer to רבי ירמיה's question about the בכור whose ear was cut: the son is not fined.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: נָקְטִינַן,
phrases.english: And Rav Asi son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: We have a tradition:
phrases.notes: An accepted tradition

phrases.english: If he improved it and died, his son may sow it.
phrases.notes: The key fact for the proof

phrases.english: So we see that the Rabbis penalized him,
phrases.notes: The father personally

phrases.english: but they did not penalize his son.
phrases.notes: The penalty ends with the father's death

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: נָקְטִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a tradition to the משנה from Step 18 and draws the conclusion that answers Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the קנס falls on the person or on the property
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי ברבי חנינא's tradition: הטיבה ומת, בנו זורעה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן fined the father himself, not his property, so the son is not penalized.

steps.title: אביי begins a tradition of his own
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens with 'We have a tradition'. The content of his tradition comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only an opening line. אביי is setting up a tradition he is about to state, and the text continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses the same word, נקטינן, that רב אסי used, so he is bringing another received tradition. We cannot judge yet whether it supports or questions the conclusion that the son is not fined. That will come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא, the student of רבה and רב יוסף

phrases.english: Abaye says: We have a tradition
phrases.notes: The content continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new tradition right after the conclusion of Step 19. Its role becomes clear on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the opening formula appears on this amud; the content of the tradition comes on the next amud.
